definitions.explanation: A secret word or phrase used to identify allies or gain entry. Historically used in military and security contexts.
A phrase adopted as the guiding principle or shared goal of a group or movement.

examples.japanese: {合言葉|あいことば}は「{山|やま}」だ。
{門番|もんばん}に{合言葉|あいことば}を{告|つ}げた。
examples.english: I told the gatekeeper the password.

examples.japanese: {合言葉|あいことば}を{知|し}らない{者|もの}は{入|はい}れない。
examples.english: Those who don't know the password cannot enter.

examples.japanese: 「{安全第一|あんぜんだいいち}」が{合言葉|あいことば}だ。
チームの{合言葉|あいことば}は「{全力|ぜんりょく}」だ。
examples.english: The team's rallying cry is 'give it your all.'

examples.japanese: 「{変革|へんかく}」を{合言葉|あいことば}に{新|あたら}しい{取|と}り{組|く}みが{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: A new initiative was launched under the rallying cry of 'reform.'

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {合言葉|あいことば}を{決|き}める (set a password/motto)
- {合言葉|あいことば}を{告|つ}げる (tell the password)
- 〜を{合言葉|あいことば}に (with ~ as a motto/rallying cry)

USAGE:
The sense 1 usage (password) evokes historical or fantasy settings — guards at castle gates, secret societies, etc. For modern digital passwords, パスワード is the standard term. The sense 2 usage (motto/rallying cry) is common in modern Japanese, especially in business, sports, and community contexts.
